title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is setting up a Dold–Kan-type dictionary between simplicial objects and (co)chain complexes, as groundwork for a divided-power de Rham complex attached to the simplices.

The key object is the normalized cochain complex of the standard simplex. A nondegenerate i-simplex of Δ^n is an (i+1)-element subset of [n] = {0,…,n}. Hence
C^i(Δ^n) ≅ Λ^{i+1}(k^{Δ^n}), where k^{Δ^n} = k^{n+1} is the space of functions on the vertices.
The coboundary δ(e_S) = Σ_{j∉S} ± e_{S∪{j}} is wedging with Γ_n = Σ_j e_j. So C^·(Δ^n) is the Koszul complex of the pair (k^{Δ^n}, Γ_n).
Dually, the normalized chains C_·(Δ^n) = N k[Δ^n] are Λ^{·+1} of the dual space, with boundary the interior product by the augmentation.
In Grothendieck's notation, C^·_{[n]} = Λ^{·+1} L_{[n]} = Λ^{·+1} k^{Δ^n} and C_·^{[n]} = Λ^{·+1} Ľ_{[n]}. As n varies these form a cosimplicial complex and a simplicial complex.

Step 1 (Yoneda through Dold–Kan).
- For a simplicial k-module λ_*, Hom_k(k[Δ^n_*], λ_*) = Hom(Δ^n_*, λ_*) = λ_{[n]}.
- Take λ = C_*(Δ^m). Then Hom of complexes from C_·^{[n]} to C_·(Δ^m) equals Hom of simplicial modules from k[Δ^n] to k[Δ^m], by Dold–Kan full faithfulness.
- This equals k[Hom_Δ([n],[m])] = k^{(Hom(Δ_n, Δ_m))}.
- He also writes the dual cochain statement: Hom^·(Λ^{·+1}k^{Δ^n}, Λ^{·+1}k^{Δ^m}) as a cosimplicial object.
- So chain maps between simplex (co)chain complexes are exactly formal k-linear combinations of simplicial maps.

Step 2 (the warning 'pas linéaire!').
- A map f: [n]→[m] induces pull-back f^*: k^{Δ^m} → k^{Δ^n}, with f^*Γ_m = Γ_n. So f gives a morphism of pointed vector spaces (k^{Δ_m}, Γ_m) → (k^{Δ_n}, Γ_n).
- Applying Λ^{·+1} to such a morphism gives a chain map of Koszul complexes. This works even for arbitrary set maps, matching the Hom_ens on the previous page.
- But the map f ↦ (f^*, then Λ(f^*)) does not extend linearly. The Γ-preserving linear maps form an affine, not linear, subspace, and Λ is polynomial (not linear) in f^*.
- The correct linear map k^{(Hom)} → Hom(Λ k^{Δ_m}, Λ k^{Δ_n}) is therefore defined on the basis f ↦ Λ(f^*), extended linearly; it does not factor linearly through Hom_k((k^{Δ_m},Γ_m),(k^{Δ_n},Γ_n)).

Purpose: to describe the cosimplicial cochain complex of simplices and its endomorphism (Hom) structure functorially. This prepares the analogous description of the (divided-power) de Rham complex of the algebraic simplices, which is the topic of the 1976 IHÉS talk.
errors: The identification 'Hom of complexes = k[Hom(Δ^n,Δ^m)]' holds for order-preserving maps (Dold–Kan full faithfulness). The previous page uses Hom_ens (all set maps), and Λ^{·+1} is functorial in all set maps. The two indexing sets are conflated in places; the chain maps Λ(f^*) for non-monotone f do lie in the span, but not as new basis elements.
Products k^{Hom} and direct sums k^{(Hom)} are used interchangeably. This is harmless since all sets are finite.
The last line duplicates Δ_m (transcription or slip); it should be Hom(Λ k^{Δ_m}, Λ k^{Δ_n}) to match the arrow above it.

ideas.what: Normalized cochains of Δ^n identified with Λ^{·+1}(k^{n+1}), with differential given by wedging with Γ = Σ e_i (a Koszul complex)
ideas.modern_name: Koszul/exterior-algebra model of simplicial (co)chains of the standard simplex

ideas.what: Chain maps between normalized chain complexes of simplices ≅ k[Hom_Δ([n],[m])] via Yoneda plus Dold–Kan
ideas.modern_name: Dold–Kan full faithfulness / Yoneda for simplicial modules

ideas.what: Remark that f ↦ Λ(f^*), via Γ-preserving linear maps, is not linear: linear combinations of simplicial maps are not maps of pointed vector spaces

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine bookkeeping: the Koszul-complex description of simplex cochains and Dold–Kan/Yoneda. It is a working step toward the divided-power de Rham talk, with no new result or overlooked connection on this page.
transcription_corrections: The last formula should most likely read Hom(Λ^{·+1}k^{Δ_m}, Λ^{·+1}k^{Δ_n}), not Λ k^{Δ_m} twice.
Exponents written '·+1' appear in the image as '*+1' / '·+1' over Λ, consistent with the previous page.

The underlined captions under the Hom lines read roughly 'comme ... cosimpl. cat' and 'comme simpl. ... cat'. They are only partially legible; a plausible reading is 'en tant que (co)simpl. ab./cat.'.
Top line: the right-hand term reads k^{Hom(Δ^n, Δ^{m})} (possibly Δ^{n-1}). The arrow is drawn as a curved arrow pointing to the left term.
